title: Subbing for Begard and Alexander and joining Bernard's band
summary: After stopping lessons, he subs for clarinetists in Homer Begard's group and is invited into Bernard's band as a regular.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Yeah, well, yeah, he used the book. You see, after I left Walter Defining, well, you know, I went to Louie. Louie, there were some things that I had the wrong understanding about the division, and Louie straightened me out on that. And, well, I got out of work. I wasn't paying much, but I got out of work. So I thought, I said, well, Louie, I'm not coming for lessons right now because I'm not working. I won't be able to pay you. He said, well, that don't stop you from coming. I said, well, no, I don't want to be that way. So I just stopped going to him, you see. And when I went back to work, well, I still didn't go back there. So I got to playing around with little bands. And there was Bonnie Begard and Adolph Alexander. They was playing with a band by the name of Homer Begard. It was a trumpet player. You ever heard of him?
I knew of Emil Begard. That was Barney Sunko on violin.
No, this was a trumpet player, Homer Begard. I don't remember.
I've heard of him, but I don't remember.

Well, them guys just played with him. And, well, every time they get a job, they had a little more. They'd look for somebody to sit in their place. So a lot of the time they came and got me. Well, when I first stopped out, the fellas, when them fellas see me coming, they'd get angry. Because they couldn't play anything.
That was some kid that wasn't as experienced.

So, well, they kept sending me in their place. And I just kept practicing. And every time playing a number, I remember the key it was in. And I practiced hard for the next time. They'd send me an horn like that. So I got to play most of the numbers that they would play. So I'm a big guy, I saw him, Bernard, he told me, he said, listen, he said, you want to join my band? He said, if them fellas can send you in their place and you can make out on them jobs, he said, well, you can be in the band regular. I said, well, that's up to you. I said, well, all right. Now you're a member of the band. So I got to playing with them. I played with them a long time. And, well, he used to get a lot of work. And until I got something better, I'd forgotten.
